assessment: This study investigated the mechanisms that underlie chronic tendinopathies. The authors identified the role of galvanic current on cellular death and inflammation in vitro and its association with tendinopathy in vivo. They showed that galvanic current induces NLRP3 inflammasome-driven low-grade inflammatory response, which promotes collagen-mediated regeneration of the tendon. This work may lead to a therapeutic strategy to treat chronic tendinopathies.
